title: Uniform spectral gap for the spin-2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic ring
credit: Haldane (1983) prediction; S=2 case left open after the 2026 S=1 claims
premise_risks: Active area: the S=1 proof and its extensions are Sept-Nov 2026 preprints, and a certified S=2 result could appear soon. Not currently claimed by OpenAI or Anthropic.
Special case of the person-named Haldane conjecture: allowed as an unnamed partial sub-question, but the scorer may see it as a famous problem in disguise.
If solved by pure large computation plus the existing bootstrap, it may be judged low in new ideas.
plain: Put a quantum spin of size 2 at each site of a ring of L sites (L even) and couple neighbours by the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg interaction; the Hamiltonian is an explicit Hermitian matrix of size 5^L whose lowest eigenvalue is simple. Prove that the gap between the lowest and second-lowest eigenvalue stays above a fixed positive constant for all even L. The spin-1 case was proved in 2026 by a computer-assisted method; for spin 2 the predicted gap is only about 0.088 and the correlation length about 50 sites.
math: Let $S^x,S^y,S^z$ be the spin-2 matrices on $\mathbb C^5$ and, for even $L\ge 4$, $H_L=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z}\vec S_i\cdot\vec S_{i+1}$ acting on $(\mathbb C^5)^{\otimes L}$, with eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) $\lambda_1(L)\le\lambda_2(L)\le\cdots$. Prove that $\inf_{L\ \mathrm{even},\,L\ge4}\big(\lambda_2(L)-\lambda_1(L)\big)>0$.
